art.why: Congregation or church interior: Daumier's In Church (reformation), Saenredam (defence-of-the-west) and Panini's Pantheon (come-and-see) were claimed first; the church interiors by Neeffs, de Witte and Pannini are used.

art.title: The Baptism of Christ
art.why: Jesus hip-deep in the river, John on the bank, two angels, and a bearded figure above in blue: the Father, Son (and Spirit) of Matthew 28:19 in one picture. Check the description for the dove before saying so.
No preacher free (Catlin's Kickapoo preaching has no gallery description; the Dominican preaching is claimed).

art.title: The Last Supper
art.why: Thirteen at a long table, Christ in a gold starburst: the meal at the heart of worship. Existing id, used only by the story bank.

art.title: Portrait of a Quaker
art.why: A plain portrait of an eighteenth-century Quaker against a dark ground, for Barclay's case for silent worship. No Quaker meeting is in the NGA. (The sitter is unnamed; the gallery's description notes gold buttons, which Stage B should not over-read.)
No Mass of St Gregory or Eucharist scene in the NGA open data.
Church interior full of light: Panini's Pantheon claimed by come-and-see; the others are used.

music.why: A hymn for the first day of the week, to the Trinity.

Psalm 23, as the word is sung in worship.
A eucharistic motet: the body given.
Whittier's Quaker poem 'the silence of eternity': the case for silence.
A motet on mystery: the Orthodox answer to what the bread is.
Handel's anthem sung at every British coronation since 1727: the glory of public worship.
